text:
anil: braindump after today's scheduler pairing. goal: tighten the scheduler<->batcher contract without adding too many RPCs.
sophia: Nice. main pain from perf run was reclaim-induced p99 spikes. We need a path that lets scheduler safely expect capacity without forcing compaction often.
ben: We should define 3 escalation levels: 0) passive metrics, 1) shaping/coalesce hint, 2) reclaim with credits token. Keep reclaim as last resort.
tara: +1. Also add a short TTL on credit tokens to avoid hoarding. Maybe 250ms by default.
anil: thinking of semantics:
- metrics stream (100-250ms): {lane, occupancy, head_gap_ms, compactness}
- shaping RPC: best-effort, quick response (true/false, est_freed)
- reclaim RPC: async, returns job_id -> ack carries credits_token + freed_count + reserve_ms
ben: small nit: metrics should include "reserved_for_scheduler" count so scheduler knows what's already promised.
sophia: and include an ownership_version so scheduler can detect lane owner changes and cancel in-flight reclaim.
tara: about idempotency: reclaim must accept an idempotency_key and return same job_id if retried. prevents double work on network blips.
anil: good. Also need a cancel endpoint: `POST /reclaim/cancel` that takes job_id and lease_token. If ownership moves, scheduler cancels outstanding jobs. Batcher must be able to safely abort and report partial frees.
ben: recovery story: if batcher fails after ack but before TTL expires, scheduler should be resilient. Use an immutable credits_token that batcher redeems once scheduler claims; but if batcher crashes, it should persist tokens until TTL. Edge: if token disappears, scheduler times out and re-evaluates.
sophia: Observability: emit `shaping.request`, `shaping.response`, `reclaim.started`, `reclaim.partial`, `reclaim.finished`, and `credits.redeem.latency`. Make them high-cardinality-tagged by lane and job_id.
tara: rollout plan: 1) metrics stream + reserved count (FF off by default), 2) shaping endpoint in canary, 3) reclaim disabled but tested under lab, 4) enable reclaim in progressive canary with perf checks.
anil: perf tests: microbench with 10-50k small requests/s, bursty arrivals, lane transfer during reclaim. Measure p50/p95/p99 before/after.
ben: one more behavioural thought: scheduler should prefer consuming "reserved" slots (credits tokens) before taking new admits. avoids racing with other schedulers.
sophia: Implementation detail: keep credits token tiny and opaque, include `amount:int` and `expires_at_ms`. Batcher persists (job_id -> token) until expiry. Dedup logic must live in batcher.
tara: Also add a "shaping_hint_duration_ms" in shaping response so scheduler knows how long shaped state is expected to hold. Helps hysteresis.
anil: Security note: lease_token must be signed by scheduler (or include nonce) to avoid cross-tenant misuse. ops-bot, file a dependency ticket for auth headers for these endpoints.
ops-bot: created-ticket: AUTH-4823 "Batcher RPC auth headers for reclaim/shaping" assigned to platform-security.
ben: ok action items: anil -> write mini-RFC with proto examples and failure cases; sophia -> telemetry list + dashboard mockups; tara -> perf harness scenarios; I'll pair on batcher persistence API.
sophia: will include a sample proto snippet in RFC and a simulation of token TTL impact.
tara: let's be conservative with enabling reclaim in prod. shaping should buy us most wins.
anil: thanks all. will post RFC link and ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
